disclaimer: Research aid, not legal advice. Items marked 'reported' come from secondary summaries; 'unresearched' markets need local counsel.

regimes.eu-optout: Commercial TDM allowed unless the rightsholder reserved it 'in an appropriate manner, such as machine-readable means' (DSM Directive 2019/790 Art. 4(3)); GPAI providers must honour reservations (AI Act Art. 53(1)(c)).
regimes.no-optout-exception: Broad TDM/AI exception with no rightsholder opt-out; protection relies on access conditions, technical measures or the exception's limits.
regimes.fair-use: No statutory TDM rule; AI training judged case by case under fair use / fair dealing.
regimes.no-exception: No TDM exception for commercial AI training: training on protected works needs a licence or another exception.

EU.name: European Union (baseline)
EU.law: DSM Directive 2019/790 Art. 4(3); AI Act Art. 53(1)(c) (fines from 2 Aug 2026); GPAI Code of Practice copyright chapter, Measure 1.3 (robots.txt per RFC 9309 mandatory, other protocols best-effort)
EU.named_bot_risk: In a Dutch case where the robots.txt named only some AI bots, the court found the scraper was not effectively excluded; commentators read it as requiring the opt-out to target the bots concerned (Rb Amsterdam, 30 Oct 2024, ECLI:NL:RBAMS:2024:6563; appeal reported pending).
EU.labelling: AI Act Art. 50(4): deployers disclose deepfakes and AI-generated text on matters of public interest unless human-reviewed under editorial responsibility; applies 2 Aug 2026.

DE.name: Germany
DE.law: §44b UrhG (reservation for online works effective only if machine-readable, §44b(3)); §60d research
DE.cases: OLG Hamburg 10 Dec 2025, 5 U 104/24 (Kneschke v LAION: appeal dismissed, the reservation was reported as not demonstrably machine-readable, use also covered by §60d; revision to the BGH allowed); LG München I 11 Nov 2025, 42 O 14139/24 (GEMA v OpenAI: memorisation is reproduction)

FR.name: France
FR.law: Art. L.122-5-3 CPI; Senate bill on a presumption of use of works by AI (TA n°85, 8 Apr 2026) pending at the National Assembly

IT.name: Italy
IT.law: Arts. 70-ter, 70-quater LDA; Art. 70-septies (Law 132/2025, in force 10 Oct 2025); Art. 171(1)(a-ter) criminalises unlawful TDM

ES.name: Spain
ES.law: TRLPI transposition of DSM Art. 4; draft AI law with labelling fines (not in force)

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.cases: Rb Amsterdam 30 Oct 2024 (DPG Media v HowardsHome; appeal reported pending)

UK.name: United Kingdom
UK.law: CDPA s29A (non-commercial research only; contract override void s29A(5)); government report of 18 Mar 2026 shelved an opt-out exception
UK.search: CMA conduct requirement (3 Jun 2026): Google must let publishers opt out of AI Overviews / AI Mode at directory then page level without ranking penalty (reported deadlines Dec 2026 / Mar 2027).
UK.cases: Getty v Stability [2025] EWHC 2863 (Ch); appeal pending

US.name: United States
US.law: 17 USC §107; Bartz v Anthropic (2025, $1.5bn settlement approved Jul 2026); Kadrey v Meta (2025); Thomson Reuters v Ross (3d Cir. 29 Sep 2026, not fair use)
US.labelling: California SB 942 (operative 2 Aug 2026 via AB 853) binds large GenAI providers, not publishers

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.law: Art. 24d CopA (scientific research only); revision under consultation

JP.name: Japan
JP.law: Copyright Act Art. 30-4 (non-enjoyment uses incl. commercial) unless use 'unreasonably prejudices' rightsholders
JP.named_bot_risk: Agency for Cultural Affairs, General Understanding (15 Mar 2024): circumventing robots.txt or other technical measures protecting a database offered for analysis may trigger the proviso; RAG outputs may fall outside Art. 30-4.
JP.cases: Yomiuri, Nikkei & Asahi v Perplexity (Tokyo District Court, filed Aug 2025)

SG.name: Singapore
SG.law: Copyright Act 2021 ss243-244 (computational data analysis, lawful access required); s187 voids contract terms excluding s244

CN.name: China
CN.law: Copyright Law Art. 24 (closed list, no TDM exception)
CN.labelling: CAC Measures for Labelling AI-Generated Synthetic Content + GB 45438-2025, effective 1 Sep 2025 (visible + metadata labels, platforms must detect)

IN.name: India
IN.law: Copyright Act s52(1)(a)(i) fair dealing; ANI v OpenAI (Delhi HC, 24 Jul 2026, interim injunction refused); DPIIT working paper proposes a statutory licence
IN.labelling: IT Amendment Rules 2026 (G.S.R. 120(E), in force 20 Feb 2026): labels + provenance metadata for synthetically generated audio-visual content

KR.name: South Korea
KR.law: Copyright Act Art. 35-5 general fair use
KR.labelling: AI Basic Act Art. 31 (in force 22 Jan 2026): operators label generative-AI outputs; fines deferred at least one year

TW.name: Taiwan
TW.law: No TDM exception; AI Basic Act (Dec 2025) creates none

AU.name: Australia
AU.law: Government ruled out a TDM exception (Oct 2025); licensing approach

CA.name: Canada
CA.law: Fair dealing s29; news publishers v OpenAI pending (Ontario)

IL.name: Israel
IL.law: Ministry of Justice opinion (18 Dec 2022): ML training typically fair use (s19)

VN.name: Vietnam
VN.law: IP Law amended by Law 131/2025/QH15 Art. 7(5) (from 1 Apr 2026); Decree 134/2026/ND-CP Art. 37b: reservation via machine-readable metadata, technical protection, rights-management information or collective declaration
VN.labelling: AI Law 134/2025/QH15 (from 1 Mar 2026): machine-readable marking of AI audio, images, video

BR.name: Brazil
BR.law: PL 2338/2023 (Senate Dec 2024; Arts. 62-65, remuneration Art. 65) pending in the Chamber

TH.name: Thailand
TH.law: Draft AI law principles: TDM exception with reservation for commercial use (not enacted)
